rationale: This is largely a re-parameterization of the archived "Financing Regime Turn" (indicator→continuous profitability weight, total financing→equity-only) layered on the well-documented net-share-issuance/composite-issuance anomaly, so it risks being a cosmetic variant rather than a substantively new mechanism.

The construction is internally consistent (nonnegative issuance exposure times signed accrual gap, expected negative), but it is close to the documented external-financing/accruals overlap (Bradshaw-Richardson-Sloan, Sloan), and the large mass point at sstk≈0 will concentrate most firms at a neutral value, limiting incremental information.

A legitimate level-versus-change diagnostic on the archive's strongest result, but note the coverage delta mechanically contains −Δ(payout), so firms ramping distributions are penalized in a way that partly contradicts the payout-increase channel the hypothesis invokes.

Swapping ni for oiadp in the archived per-share realization signal is a cosmetic input substitution of an already-known earnings-growth/earnings-momentum predictor, and the per-share dollar level is not scale-free across firms so its first difference is dominated by price/share-count scale that industry z-scoring only partially removes.

The stated refinancing/maturity-structure mechanism requires a debt-mix ratio such as dlc/(dlc+dltt), but the expression's at-dominated denominator makes it essentially short-term-debt-to-assets leverage, so the signal reduces to a familiar high-profitability/low-leverage quality composite rather than the claimed maturity channel.

A genuinely cross-theme and internally coherent interaction (nonnegative R&D-intensity weight times signed internal-versus-external funding balance) whose components are individually known but whose conditioning is a defensible financing-constraint mechanism, with the main caveat that COALESCE(xrd,0) pools true zeros with non-reporters.
